title: A pid file that outlives a host reboot can make stop signal an unrelated process
foundBy: session agent, while reading internal/engine/firecracker_proc.go and internal/forward/forward.go

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/engine/ ./internal/forward/ -count=1: TestAReusedVMMPidIsNotTheMicroVM and TestAReusedForwardPidIsDeadAndNeverSignalled PASS. Each points a record at a live `sleep`, which the old code reported running and killed. On a real microVM with fc.pid pointed at a bystander `sleep`, `ls` reported stopped and `stop` left the bystander alive. The full `make ci` gate on the six commits together exited 0, with 14 of 14 agent replay cells passing on podman. `make test-agents-lent AGENTS_ENGINE=firecracker` passed 7 of 7.

resolution: cs-sandbox records each tracked process's start time beside its pid and signals it only through a pidfd, after checking the start time and argv still match (R170). A record that fails the check counts as dead and is never signalled.
details:
Two places decide a tracked process is alive by sending signal 0 to a recorded pid, and neither checks that the process is the one they recorded. `fcRunning` reads `<instance>/fc.pid` for a microVM (`internal/engine/firecracker_proc.go:132`). `alive` reads the pid out of a forward record for a detached `ssh -N` child (`internal/forward/forward.go:244`).

Both records live under the instances directory, which survives a host reboot, and nothing sweeps them at boot. Linux issues pids from a counter that restarts low after a reboot and wraps, so a number recorded before the reboot can belong to something else after it.

The consequences follow from the check alone. `cs-sandbox ls` reports a dead microVM as running, `start` refuses it as already up, and `stop` sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to whatever now holds the number (`killFirecracker`). `unforward`, `rm` and `destroy` reach the same code for forwards. The victim is another process of yours, because a pid you can signal is one you own.

Reproduce it by creating a Firecracker sandbox, rebooting the host, and comparing `cat <instance>/fc.pid` against `ps -p <pid>`. Recording the process start time from field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` beside the pid, and requiring both to match, closes it without a new dependency.
